clue.text: Runners could not see their endless punishment

definitions.text: Runners could not see their endless punishment

parts.words: Runners could not see their endless punishment
parts.note: the nursery rhyme's sightless rodents ran after the farmer's wife, who cut off their tails with a carving knife, leaving them literally without ends

explanation.surface: Some athletes, somehow blinded, suffer a punishment that never stops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' reads as 'never-ending', but here it means 'tail-less': the farmer's wife docked the tails of the three running rodents in the English nursery rhyme.
explanation.definitionFit: The nursery-rhyme trio are sightless runners whose punishment was losing their tails.

clue.text: The last place to start ship's bingo

indicators.note: only the opening stretch of the word for the game is wanted, so its later letters are dropped

parts.note: tombola is a raffle-style numbers game, the name used for bingo in the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: A sailor names the final venue for the ship's bingo night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to start' drops OLA from TOMBOLA, the Navy's name for bingo. The grid's TOME looks like a misprint.
explanation.definitionFit: A grave is where a person is finally laid to rest, their last resting place.

clue.text: Is swine's head included in part of the menu ?

definitions.text: Is swine's head included in part of the menu

indicators.note: the phrase signals that the opening pieces go inside the word for a part

parts.note: an actor's part is a role

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, here the start of swine's

explanation.surface: A diner asks whether pig's head features somewhere on the menu.
explanation.walkthrough: 'included in' signals the container and 'head' takes the first letter of 'swine's'. Read whole, the clue also describes the dish itself, a meat patty on a menu.
explanation.definitionFit: A fried patty of minced meat is a standard item on a cafe menu, and it may well contain pork.

clue.text: Liner wrecked with gales — BM display

definitions.text: Liner wrecked with gales — BM display

indicators.note: a wrecked ship is broken apart, so these letters are smashed and reassembled

parts.note: the letters stand for the British Museum

explanation.surface: A ship is broken up by storms, and its wreckage ends up as a museum exhibit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrecked' rearranges LINER, GALES and BM together. The British Museum (BM) in London displays these Parthenon sculptures, so the whole clue also defines the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Parthenon sculptures Lord Elgin brought to Britain are a famous exhibit in the British Museum.

clue.text: Meal when Trotsky accepts a French honour

indicators.note: taking something in means holding it inside, so the name goes around the other pieces

parts.note: the Russian revolutionary's first name was Leon
un is the French for a
CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British award

explanation.surface: A diner records when the Russian revolutionary is given a French decoration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when' is a link. CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order, and Trotsky's first name was Leon.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal word for a midday meal, as served at an official function.

clue.text: Where parliamentarians won new base in Empire State

indicators.note: the shuffled letters are placed inside the abbreviation for the state

parts.note: the Empire State is a nickname for New York, NY

indicators.note: something new is made over, so the letters of base are rearranged

explanation.surface: A history note on a new military base built in New York.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' signals the anagram and 'in' the container. Naseby, in Northamptonshire, was a decisive Parliamentarian victory over Charles I in the English Civil War (1645).
explanation.definitionFit: The Battle of Naseby in 1645 was where Cromwell's New Model Army defeated the Royalists.

clue.text: See 1
At home, with meals, in Hull

parts.note: someone who is at home is in
board means meals provided, as in bed and board

explanation.surface: A traveller staying with meals provided in the Yorkshire port of Hull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hull' looks like the city in Yorkshire, but the capital is there only to disguise a ship's hull.
explanation.definitionFit: Something positioned within a vessel's hull, rather than outside it, is inboard.

clue.text: Breakfast chocolate literally often in this form

definitions.text: Breakfast chocolate literally often in this form

parts.words: Breakfast chocolate literally often in this form
parts.note: eggs are a breakfast food, and the chocolate sold for a spring festival usually comes shaped as eggs

explanation.surface: A remark that breakfast and chocolate both often take the same shape.
explanation.walkthrough: Chocolate for the spring festival is usually egg-shaped, and eggs are literally breakfast food.
explanation.definitionFit: Chocolate confections given at the spring festival are traditionally shaped like eggs.

clue.text: Fair reward for bravery would not please him

definitions.text: Fair reward for bravery would not please him

parts.words: Fair reward for bravery would not please him
parts.note: the saying runs that only the brave deserve the fair, and the fair sex as a prize would not suit a man who dislikes women

explanation.surface: A just prize for courage would leave a certain man unimpressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fair' seems to mean 'just', but it is 'the fair', meaning women, as in 'none but the brave deserves the fair'.
explanation.definitionFit: A man who hates women would not want them as his prize.

clue.text: One gets an encore abroad, or the bird

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I
bis is the French and Italian call for an encore

explanation.surface: A performer either earns an encore overseas or gets booed off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the bird' looks like jeering a performer off stage (getting the bird), but it is the definition: a wading bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-legged wading bird with a curved bill, sacred in ancient Egypt.

clue.text: Joining up of speech

parts.note: the word covers both the jointing of bones or parts and the clear forming of spoken sounds

explanation.surface: A phrase about stringing words together into fluent speech.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a joint between parts and the clear pronunciation of words.

clue.text: Self-defining part of speech

parts.note: the grammatical label for a naming word is itself a naming word, so it describes its own class

explanation.surface: A grammar lesson on a word class that names itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A naming word is a word class whose own name belongs to that class.

clue.text: Winter possibly 'ere in Bath

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters could be put in another arrangement

explanation.surface: A Cockney remarks that winter might be spent here in the spa town of Bath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges ERE, IN and BATH. 'Winter' is a verb here: to spend the winter.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass the cold season asleep or dormant, as a hedgehog does.

clue.text: Sixth form introduction to University

definitions.meaning: the top year of a British secondary school is its highest class
the first letter of University is U, the label for ... usage in the U and non-U distinction

explanation.surface: A school's top year prepares pupils for their first taste of university.
explanation.walkthrough: The sixth form is the final years at a British secondary school. U, from Nancy Mitford's 'U and non-U', marks upper-class speech.
explanation.definitionFit: A school's senior forms are its highest classes, and U is shorthand for aristocratic usage.

clue.text: " Let us pray "—sound advice he accepts

definitions.text: " Let us pray "—sound advice he accepts

parts.words: " Let us pray "—sound advice he accepts
parts.note: the church call heard by ear also sounds like an invitation to hunt victims, and a hunting animal would take that advice

explanation.surface: A congregation is urged to pray, and one listener takes the counsel to heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound advice' reads as wise advice, but means advice as heard: 'pray' sounds like 'prey', which a hunter would happily do.
explanation.definitionFit: A hunting animal lives by seizing prey, so an invitation to prey suits it.

clue.text: Eagle's victim of course

parts.note: a raptor naturally hunts small birds, and on a golf course a score two under par beats one only a single stroke under

explanation.surface: Naturally a little bird falls prey to the eagle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of course' seems to mean 'naturally', but it is the golf course: an eagle (two under par) beats a birdie (one under).
explanation.definitionFit: A child's word for a small bird, and the golf score of one under par.

clue.text: Learned men have strange rite, in Latin mostly

indicators.note: the shuffled letters are placed inside the shortened language name
most of the word is kept, its final letter being dropped
something strange is out of the usual order, so the letters of rite are rearranged

explanation.surface: Scholars perform an odd ceremony conducted mostly in Latin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strange' signals the anagram, 'mostly' drops the final letter, and 'in' puts the shuffled ceremony inside what remains of the language.
explanation.definitionFit: Educated, well-read people form an intellectual elite.

clue.text: Invest first in equities having suffered reverse

indicators.note: suffering a reverse means being turned back, so the whole string is read backwards
the first letter of the word equities is taken

parts.note: having endured something is to have borne it

explanation.surface: An investor puts money into shares first, then suffers a setback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Invest' looks financial, but means clothe ceremonially. 'reverse' turns E plus BORNE into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To invest someone is to dress them in the robes of office.

clue.text: Whale reveals some of its temper or quality

indicators.note: only some of the letters of these words are used, a run lying across them

explanation.surface: A whale shows something of its temperament or character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some of' finds the run across 'tempeR OR QUALity'.
explanation.definitionFit: A rorqual is a type of baleen whale, such as the blue whale.

clue.text: Effect of silencer included in recording proceedings

indicators.note: a piece that is included sits inside another, so the short word goes in the middle

parts.note: a silencer has a muting effect, deadening sound

explanation.surface: A gun's silencer makes a difference to the record of a hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Effect of silencer' sounds like a gun, but only describes deadening sound; 'included' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking minutes is writing up an official record of a meeting.

clue.text: Examine soft inside of a hexapod

indicators.note: the musical letter is set within the word for the six-legged creature

parts.note: a hexapod has six legs, which every insect does
p, for piano, is the musical mark for soft

explanation.surface: Look closely at the soft innards of a six-legged creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soft inside' looks like a body part, but 'soft' is P (piano, in music) and 'inside' puts it in INSECT.
explanation.definitionFit: To inspect is to look over something carefully.

clue.text: Theatre in the flat?

parts.note: a picture house shows drama on a flat screen, in two dimensions rather than on a stage

explanation.surface: A question about putting on a play at home in a flat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the flat' suggests an apartment, but means flat, two-dimensional pictures: drama on a screen.
explanation.definitionFit: A picture house is a theatre where films are shown on a flat screen.

clue.text: White Friar's worry about me getting fired

indicators.note: one piece surrounds the others, as in going about them

parts.note: care is worry or anxiety
something fired has been set alight, lit

explanation.surface: A monk is anxious that he will be sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'White Friar's' means 'White Friar is'. 'fired' looks like dismissal, but means set alight; 'about' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of the Carmel order are called White Friars for their white cloaks.

clue.text: A capital orchestra, too!

parts.note: the London Symphony Orchestra is the LSO, an orchestra of the capital

explanation.surface: A remark that a London orchestra is present as well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' means London here: the LSO is the London Symphony Orchestra.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean in addition or as well.

clue.text: The instrument Belloc's Matilda heard

indicators.note: what is heard is the sound of the word, its spelling being different

parts.note: Hilaire Belloc's cautionary-tale Matilda told such dreadful lies that nobody believed her cries of fire

explanation.surface: A tale-teller named Matilda hears a musical instrument being played.
explanation.walkthrough: Matilda, in Belloc's poem 'Matilda, Who told Lies, and was Burned to Death', was a habitual liar. The grid's PYRE (perhaps inspired by her fiery end) looks like a misprint.
explanation.definitionFit: A small harp-like stringed instrument of ancient Greece.

clue.text: It finished off Romeo's father

indicators.note: the end of the name is what finishes it off, so only its closing letters remain

parts.note: in Shakespeare's Romeo and Juliet, Romeo's father is Lord Montague

explanation.surface: Something killed off the father of Shakespeare's lovesick hero.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finished off' seems to mean killed, and an ague (a malarial fever) could do that, but it gives the finishing letters of MONTAGUE.
explanation.definitionFit: An ague is a malarial fever, the kind of illness that could kill someone.

clue.text: How families are joined ? Absolutely not

definitions.meaning: families are linked through their kin, by blood or marriage
the opposite of absolutely is comparatively, in relation to something else

explanation.surface: A question about family ties, answered with a firm refusal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Absolutely not' looks like a refusal, but is a definition: the opposite of 'absolutely'.
explanation.definitionFit: Families are linked by kinship, and the word also means in comparison, the opposite of absolutely.

clue.text: Man at the bar has abjured the stuff

definitions.text: Man at the bar has abjured the stuff

parts.words: Man at the bar has abjured the stuff
parts.note: a senior barrister gives up the junior's gown of stuff, a woollen cloth, for one of finer material

explanation.surface: A drinker in the pub has sworn off alcohol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the bar' suggests a pub and 'the stuff' drink, but this is a barrister who has become a King's Counsel (in Britain, 'taking silk'), swapping the junior's stuff gown for one of silk.
explanation.definitionFit: A senior barrister in Britain is called a silk, after the gown worn on appointment as Queen's Counsel.

clue.text: Highly-strung performer

parts.note: a puppet worked from above is literally hung on strings high up

explanation.surface: A nervous, temperamental actor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Highly-strung' means nervous, but here it is literal: a puppet worked by strings from above.
explanation.definitionFit: A string puppet is a performer operated by strings from above.
